q7.answer: The refresh timer swaps the new value and version id into SecretStore's memory under a lock, and each provider client reads the current value from SecretStore on every call, so the next call after the swap uses the new key. A pod picks up a new version within one refresh cycle, which is 5 minutes plus up to about 30 seconds of jitter.

q8.answer: Rollout step 9 requires that every replica reports the new version id for all three names in its start-up and refresh logs and in the secret_version_info metric, that no replica runs an old image, and that provider dashboards show old-key traffic at zero for an agreed window, with a 10-minute wait after the last replacement. The length of that soak window is not decided, and whether each provider can show per-key usage is an open question.

q9.answer: Store access is set first (rollout step 2), then dev and staging values are written (step 3), then new prod keys are created at each provider and written to the store (step 4), then read access is checked as the orders-api-prod identity (step 5). The code merge then switches the app to read the store and removes the api_key lines from config/app.yaml in the same change (step 6), pods are rolled and confirmed (steps 7 to 9), and the deny policy is applied before the old keys are revoked at the providers (step 10).

q10.answer: A developer runs make run with APP_ENV=dev, and the app reads the orders-api/dev/* secrets, which hold provider sandbox or test keys, using the developer's own SSO identity orders-api-dev. Live keys never go into dev, and there is no fallback to committed keys, a local key file or prod; offline work uses recorded responses or stubs. The store product and how SSO maps to that identity are not named in the brief.

q11.answer: The process does not start serving with a partial set of keys. A missing or empty value counts as a failed read, the app retries, and if any of the three keys is still missing after the retries it logs an error naming the key and the error class (never the value) and exits with a non-zero code. How the retries apply per key, versus to the whole load, is not spelled out in the plan.
